subject: missing data when analyzing mutliple phenotype columns

messages.author: 8a1ab6778bca2593
messages.subject: missing data when analyzing mutliple phenotype columns
parts:
Hi Karl et al.

I have been getting somewhat surprising results when using scanone to analyze multiple phenotype columns at once.  My guess is that any individual that has missing phenotype data from ANY trait is dropped from the analysis of ALL traits.  Is this true, and would it be possible to have an option to change the behavior?

Thanks,

J.

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: missing data when analyzing mutliple phenotype columns
parts:
Yes, you are right. I'm sorry that this wasn't clear. I should have
the
function spit out warnings about this, at the very least.

The speed-ups we've done for Haley-Knott regression and the
imputation method
require that all individuals have all phenotypes, but it seems we
should use
the quicker approach only in the case that all individuals are
phenotyped.

karl
